grammar_focus: 虚拟条件句/非真实条件(if + 过去式, would + 动词原形;be 用 were,KS16)主考——想象、跟事实相反的情况;真实条件(if + 现在时, will / 祈使句)对比;将来进行时 will be + V-ing 委婉问将来、be busy doing、ask sb to do、in despair(辅考·课文①类)
scene: 上星期的一次宴会上,女主人安排我坐在兰伯尔德夫人身旁。兰伯尔德夫人是位身材高大、表情严肃的女人,穿一件紧身黑衣裙。我坐到她身旁时,她连头都没抬一下,眼睛盯着自己的盘子,不一会儿就忙着吃起来。我想找个话题跟她聊聊。“环球剧场就要上演一出新戏了,”我说,“您去看吗?”“不,”她回答。“您今年去国外度假吗?”我又问。“不,”她回答。“您就呆在英国吗?”我问。“不,”她回答。失望之中我问她饭菜是否合口味。“年轻人,”她回答说,“如果你多吃点、少说点,我们两个都会吃得开心的!”

grammar_card.title: 虚拟条件句:如果…就会…(说想象的情况)
grammar_card.intro: 谈想象、跟事实相反的情况:if 从句用过去式,主句用 would + 动词原形;be 一律用 were。跟真实条件(if + 现在时,主句用 will 或祈使句)区分开。全用本课和 Key structures 的句子举例。

rows: If you ate more and talked less, we would both enjoy our dinner.
多吃少说,我们都会吃得开心(想象)
If you went to the exhibition, you would enjoy it.
假如你去看展览,你会喜欢的(想象)
If I were you, I would talk less.
我要是你,就会少说话(be 用 were)
真实:If I have time, I'll write to him.
有空我就给他写信(现在时→will)
真实:Please don't disturb him if he is busy.
他忙就别打扰(现在时→祈使句)

specialRules.rule: 想象、非真实的情况:if 从句用过去式,主句用 would + 动词原形。过去式在这里不表过去,只表'非真实'。
specialRules.mark: if 过去式 + would 原形

specialRules.rule: 非真实条件里 be 一律用 were,连 I / he / she 也用 were:If I were you… / If he were here…

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — Was Mrs. Rumbold a good companion at dinner?
options: No — she only said 'No' and told him to talk less
Yes — she chatted happily all evening
Yes — she loved discussing the theater
No — she left the party early

passage: Last week at a dinner party, the hostess asked me to sit next to Mrs. Rumbold. Mrs. Rumbold was a large, unsmiling lady in a tight black dress. She did not even look up when I took my seat beside her. Her eyes were fixed on her plate and in a short time, she was busy eating. I tried to make conversation. 'A new play is coming to "The Globe" soon,' I said. 'Will you be seeing it?' 'No,' she answered. 'Will you be spending your holidays abroad this year?' I asked. 'No,' she answered. 'Will you be staying in England?' I asked. 'No,' she answered. In despair, I asked her whether she was enjoying her dinner. 'Young man,' she answered, 'if you ate more and talked less, we would both enjoy our dinner!'
